clue.text: Take bill to the bank, say the popular press

indicators.note: say tells the solver that the phrase before it is only an approximate match by its pronunciation

parts.note: a bill is a TAB, and taking it to the bank is to have it LODGED there, so: tab lodged

explanation.surface: A tip about banking a bill, offered by the mass-circulation papers.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound match is loose: 'tab lodged' said quickly is close to the plural word for downmarket newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-format sensational newspapers are collectively the popular press in Britain.

clue.text: Managed science in race to copy

indicators.note: in places managed and science inside the race word

parts.note: a tribe is a race of people
managed means ran
SC is the abbreviation for science, as in BSc

explanation.surface: A science department organised to imitate a racial group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' tempts as the definition, but it supplies the container; 'copy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To write out in full from another source is to copy it.

clue.text: Costers from Cumbria?

parts.note: costers are street traders selling from handcarts; whimsically, lads from Cumbria's town of Barrow-in-Furness

explanation.surface: Street traders from the north-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Costermongers sold from carts; Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria, England, giving the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Costers are street sellers pushing handcarts, the market traders this phrase names.

clue.text: Mass unit, formerly about turn

indicators.note: about means the formerly word goes around the turn letter

parts.note: formerly means once
U is a turn, as in U-turn

explanation.surface: An old weight unit that has done an about-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: ONCE goes about U: O(U)NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: This imperial unit of mass is one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: Unhappy with record playing long after hours?

parts.note: a record is a disc
on means playing, as a record is on
long after the expected hour is so late

explanation.surface: Gloomy because a record is still playing in the small hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link; the pieces are DISC, ON and SO LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deeply downcast, beyond comfort, is to be very unhappy.

clue.text: After starting slim get buxom — it's probably from lack of vegetables

definitions.text: it's probably from lack of vegetables

indicators.note: After places the buxom piece behind the opening letter in the answer
starting picks out only the opening letter of the word slim

parts.note: to get buxom is to become curvy, shapely

explanation.surface: Dieting then filling out, a disease that comes from eating no greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a charade signal: CURVY comes after S, the start of 'slim'.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease caused by vitamin C deficiency often arises when fresh vegetables and fruit are lacking.

clue.text: Where to keep in form

parts.note: reads like a gym for fitness, but 'keep in' is detention and 'form' is a school class

explanation.surface: A place for staying fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep in form' suggests fitness; in British schools 'form' is a class and 'keep in' means detain after lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A room where a school class is taught and kept is a teaching room.

clue.text: Take any direction — always ending here, they say

indicators.note: they say signals both a proverb and a word heard rather than spelt

parts.note: all roads lead to Rome, the city where every route ends

explanation.surface: Wander anywhere, since every road ends in one place, as the proverb goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'all roads lead to Rome' gives the city, which is said like a word for wander.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander freely without a fixed route is to go in any direction.

clue.text: Burden the old carry all right?

indicators.note: carry means the old word holds the other inside

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Can an old load be borne safely?
explanation.walkthrough: YE carries OK: Y(OK)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy oppressive load is a burden, as in the yoke of tyranny.

clue.text: Adjusted as rise in ventilation

indicators.note: Adjusted means rearranged, so the three short words are reordered into a new word

explanation.surface: A thermostat tweak as warm air rises in a ventilation system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusted' rearranges the eight letters of AS RISE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Airiness is the quality of being well aired, which is what good ventilation produces.

clue.text: It takes a lawyer to conceal material

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer
to conceal is to mask

explanation.surface: A hint that a lawyer is needed to hide some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It takes' is only a link joining the two pieces; DA is the American District Attorney.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, a kind of material.

clue.text: PM recently meeting HM for soup — or soap?

parts.note: Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister at the time
Her Majesty the Queen, of the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: Politician and monarch dining together on soup, or washing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was Prime Minister in 2010; the Royal Family's house is Windsor. Brown Windsor is a traditional British meat soup and a brown soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick brown meat broth of Victorian Britain, also a brand of brown toilet soap.

clue.text: Directors in twenties indicate the state of play

definitions.note: a verb phrase, read as 'things that indicate the state of play', the plural noun

indicators.note: in places the directors piece inside the word for twenties

parts.note: a score is twenty, so twenties are scores
a company's directors form its boards

explanation.surface: Company directors in their twenties show how the game stands.
explanation.walkthrough: SCORES is cut open by BOARDS: SCORE(BOARD)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Boards displaying the score tell spectators how a match currently stands.

clue.text: Papal pronouncement taken for granted?

definitions.meaning: the dogma, defined by Pius XII in 1950, that Mary was taken bodily into heaven

explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic doctrine proclaimed by the Pope, and a belief accepted without proof.

clue.text: Smart lady takes Gordius up — they were seen at the flicks

definitions.text: they were seen at the flicks

parts.note: U means upper-class, smart
she is a lady

indicators.note: up reverses the setter piece, read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Gordius is the setter of this puzzle

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman lifts the crossword compiler, at the cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is only a link; SETTER turned up gives RETTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who showed patrons to seats were once a familiar sight in cinemas.

clue.text: Fanatical attack captures bridgehead

indicators.note: captures means the attack word holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: a raid is an attack
the head of bridge is its first letter, B

explanation.surface: A frenzied assault that seizes a bridgehead in war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridgehead' is read as the head (first letter) of 'bridge', B, which goes inside RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means extreme and zealous in opinion, as in a rabid supporter.

clue.text: Parliament etc is stupidly trying to determine what's good for you

definitions.text: trying to determine what's good for you

parts.note: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in Japan

indicators.note: stupidly suggests disorder, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Parliament and the like are clumsily trying to legislate healthy living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' rearranges ETC IS into ETICS.
explanation.definitionFit: The science of nutrition works out which foods are healthy.

clue.text: Cutting supports spotted animals

parts.note: spotted means saw, past tense of see
horses are animals

explanation.surface: Cuttings of stock that hold up dappled creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Trestles that hold timber while it is sawn are the frames called by this name.

clue.text: Cook cabbage — it's said to be a scientific principle

indicators.note: it's said shows the words before are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to cook is to boil, and slaw is shredded cabbage

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip about cabbage claimed to be grounded in physics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boil slaw' sounds like the physicist Robert Boyle's name plus 'law'.
explanation.definitionFit: This gas law, relating pressure and volume, is a scientific principle named after Robert Boyle.

clue.text: Meditate about nothing that works with a computer

indicators.note: about means the meditate word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to muse is to meditate
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Contemplating the void beside a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointing device moved by hand is used to work a computer.

clue.text: Cox perhaps showing early disobedience?

definitions.meaning: Cox's Orange Pippin is a variety of dessert fruit for eating raw
Eve's first sin in Eden was biting the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: An apple variety alongside the first act of defiance in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: Cox is the English dessert apple, not a person; the second reading is Eve in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cox is an example of a dessert fruit, as opposed to a cooker.

clue.text: Girl takes exercise to show flexibility

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: A girl takes up gym classes to become supple.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust oneself to new conditions is to be flexible.

clue.text: Rome's fateful date in Gobi desert

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the words Gobi desert

explanation.surface: A fateful Roman date in an Asian desert.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar was killed on the Ides of March.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle of the month in the Roman calendar; on the March one Caesar was assassinated.

clue.text: You singularly show small tolerance

definitions.meaning: a thousandth of an inch, used for engineering tolerances

explanation.surface: A tiny measurement for one person.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic singular you, and engineers' slang for a thousandth of an inch.

clue.text: Every day reports a bloomer

indicators.note: reports signals a word heard rather than written

parts.note: every day means daily

explanation.surface: Daily news reports a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flower; the British say the flower's name rather like 'daily-a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden plant grown for its flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: "Siesta" — PC device for one dodging reality

indicators.note: device suggests a contrivance or scheme, so the letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An afternoon nap and a computer, a way out for someone avoiding life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device' rearranges SIESTA plus PC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seeks distraction from unpleasant facts is avoiding the real world.

clue.text: Vigorous game needs a drink

definitions.meaning: a fast racket sport played in a walled court
a sweet fruit cordial diluted with water

explanation.definitionFit: The racket game and the fruit cordial share this name.

clue.text: Attempts to carry weight at intervals

indicators.note: to carry means the attempts word holds the weight word inside it

parts.note: attempts are tries
a ton is a weight

explanation.surface: Efforts to bear a load at regular spacing.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIES carries TON: TRI(TON)ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical intervals of three whole tones are given this name.
